# Built-in tool surface

<!-- Generated by `uagent --emit-reference`. Edit the registries in
     src/, not this file; CI fails when the two disagree. -->

Descriptions are what the model reads, including the batching and budget suffixes the registry appends. `bytes` is what one schema costs in every request that advertises it, and `when` says which sessions pay it. `schema` digests the complete JSON parameters, so an argument or its description cannot change without changing this table. Conditionally registered tools are rendered from empty dependencies: the route- and skill-catalogue text a live session splices in, and MCP tools, appear in `/context` instead.

Advertised schema text totals 16318 bytes, of which 6356 bytes are sent by every session.

| `browser` | 4584 | `action, browser?, button?, close?, count?, delta_y?, element?, find?, key?, new_tab?, offset?, path?, reason?, replace?, target_id?, text?, to_element?, to_x?, to_y?, url?, view_id?, x?, y?` | yes | no | a top-level session while the web host runs the browser | `3fe6fc459bd0` | Use the shared persistent Google Chrome that the web host runs; the user sees and can drive the same browser. Access queues automatically until the previous conversation releases it or ends its turn. release when finished browsing so other threads can continue. Parallel research uses isolated signed-out browsers when enabled by the user; browser=shared requests the persistent signed-in browser. Release any current research browser before switching to shared. open, click, type (into the focused field), press, drag, scroll, back, forward and reload wait for the page to settle and return it as text: its numbered elements, its text and a view_id. click takes element (a number from a result) and that result's view_id; a number stays good on the same page, so one look serves several actions, such as filling a form in one step. click takes button=right for a context menu and count=2 for a double click. drag holds the button from element (or x and y) to to_element (or to_x and to_y), for sliders, sortable lists and drag-and-drop. press takes a key name, or one character, after any of Control, Shift, Alt and Meta joined by + (Control+A, Shift+Tab). Fill a field in one call: type with element and view_id clicks it first, replace=true overwrites what it holds, and key is pressed after. type sets a list to the option whose label it gives, and a date, time or color field to the value the page receives, such as 2027-03-12 or 19:30. read returns more: page text from offset (in characters), or with find the lines and links that contain it, whatever their case, 200 lines at a time from match offset. open takes the same offset or find and then answers as read does, for a page you only need to read; several such calls in one step read several pages. observe adds a screenshot, for a page that text does not describe; where no element number fits, click takes x and y in its CSS pixels, and scroll takes them with delta_y, each with the latest view_id. A tab opened by your action becomes active automatically; open with new_tab=true keeps the current page; tabs lists tabs, switches to target_id, and with close=true closes it instead, unless it is the current one. To look at a page you wrote, open takes path instead of url: a self-contained .html or .svg file, shown without a server (file:// URLs are refused, and its relative links do not load). upload with element, view_id and path gives a file of this conversation's folder to a file field, or to the chooser the element opens; what a page downloads lands in its downloads folder, and the next result says when the download ended. console returns the page's console messages and uncaught errors, network its requests since it loaded; find narrows both. A page's alert, confirm or prompt dialog is reported in place of the page; answer it with press Enter or Escape. A result that says SUSPECTED BLOCK means a bot check or rate limit: don't hammer it. Chrome holds the user's saved logins: on a sign-in page click the field, call fill_saved to take the one Chrome offers for it, then submit what Chrome filled. Where the user has several accounts, type the start of the wanted account's name into the field first: Chrome then offers the ones that match. Never type or repeat a password. For a login Chrome has not saved, MFA, captchas, bot checks or payment confirmation, call request_human with a reason naming the site and step; it waits until the user hands back. Never ask for credentials in chat. |
